original_test_intent: Measure approved GPU peak compute throughput in the specified precision/workload and determine whether the score meets the authoritative SKU reference without thermal, power, clock or error regression.
original_method: Obtain exact Peak TOPS tool provenance/checksum/command/config; identify GPU SKU, clocks/power mode, precision, sparsity/accumulation, operation-count formula and DA-10997-001_v31/Viking reference; drain workloads, preserve logs, baseline cooling/power/OOB; run repeated controlled samples with warmup and hard stops; compare score statistics and restore health.
manual_activity: GPU performance owner supplies authoritative SPEC/reference and approves precision/formula/threshold; operator validates cooling/power/OOB, isolates workloads and owns hard-stop recovery.
safety_requirements: Do not invent command, precision or reference
Preserve full scores and system logs
Validate cooling/redundant power/OOB before maximum load
agent_execution_scope: Run approved repeated Peak TOPS samples
Evaluate score distribution and health telemetry
Cool down, restore and report without verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It gives only a conceptual instruction, not the exact tool command/configuration required for a reproducible score.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the approved vendor command/config matching the reference, with protected full logging and synchronized telemetry.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Run a pinned workload/precision/configuration with warmup and repeated samples, compare an approved statistic to the authoritative SKU floor and record clocks/power/throttling.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Expands `check SPEC` into an attributable numeric performance experiment with safety monitoring.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A reported number cannot be judged without precision, formula and matched reference.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Sustained maximum compute can heat or brown out the system, throttle clocks, disrupt workloads or expose latent faults.
